summary: Use the API's real page-size parameter (take) instead of the generic "limit" in sync pagination defaults, and pass limitParam="take" in the nine paginated --all call sites.
reason: Quentli paginates with take/skip (default take=20). The generated determinePaginationDefaults sent limit=100, which the API ignores, so every page came back with 20 items; shortPageEndsPagination (20 < 100) then read page one as the natural end and sync stored exactly 20 rows per resource. The --all call sites passed limitParam="", so paginatedGet assumed pageSize=100 against real 20-item pages and stopped after page one for the same reason.
validated_outcome: Before: sync left customers/subscriptions/payments/invoices at exactly 20 rows each and `customers list --all` returned 20. After: `customers list --all` returns 1170, and a full re-sync stored 38192 records across 9 resources with zero warnings. Mirror counts match manual last-page probes exactly (customers 1170, subscriptions 1209, payments 22582, invoices 7655).

deferred_to_upstream.feature: The profiler should map the spec-declared page-size parameter name (take, per spec.yaml) into determinePaginationDefaults.limitParam and into the generated list call sites' limitParam argument, instead of emitting the generic "limit" / "".
deferred_to_upstream.reason: Any API whose page-size param is not literally named "limit" silently truncates both sync and --all to the first default-size page while reporting success — the worst failure mode for agent consumers.
